text:
maria: Noticed a new issue during onboarding: dotnet sample prefetch spikes cause connection pool exhaustion and 429s. Repo: https://git.redwood.dev/dotnet-prefetch (branch: prefetch-fix)
yoshi: Is this the same auth-race as other langs or something SDK-specific?
maria: Mix of both. The sample starts 12 page fetch Tasks in parallel, each task does authIfNeeded() which under current net-sdk can trigger parallel refreshes because the HttpClient is recreated per Task. When vault or token endpoint latency rises, all tasks block then retry at once. Logs:
```
[2025-03-10T11:21:02Z] Page 1 GET 200
[2025-03-10T11:21:03Z] token refresh start (Task#5)
[2025-03-10T11:21:04Z] Task#6 auth request -> queued
[2025-03-10T11:21:05Z] GET /v1/embeds?page=6 429
[2025-03-10T11:21:05Z] Retry immediate (Task#6)
[2025-03-10T11:21:08Z] token refresh complete
```
kevin: Yikes. For .NET we should recommend reusing a single HttpClient and implement a SemaphoreSlim to cap pagination concurrency. Also single-flight refresh pattern using Lazy<Task<Token>> is straightforward.
maria: My local quick fix: create a shared ApiClient injected into paginator and a SemaphoreSlim(4). Also added jittered backoff on 429 with Task.Delay(random). Eliminated the immediate retry flood.
yoshi: Can you paste the Lazy<Task> refresh snippet? people like copy/paste.
maria: snippet:
```
private Task<Token> _refreshTask;
private readonly object _refreshLock = new object();
public Task<Token> RefreshIfNeededAsync()
{
  if (!NeedsRefresh()) return Task.FromResult(currentToken);
  lock(_refreshLock)
  {
    if (_refreshTask != null) return _refreshTask;
    _refreshTask = RefreshAsync();
  }
  return _refreshTask.ContinueWith(t => { lock(_refreshLock){ _refreshTask = null; } return t.Result; });
}
```
kevin: Nice and simple. Also add client-side token-bucket limiter for outbound requests and default pagination window to 4 in sample. We should consider offering this as SDK default in a patch release.
opsbot: quota-monitor: detected spike from dotnet-onboard/org-88 in eu-central-1, applied soft-shed 40% for 90s :warning:
maria: Opsbot saved us from harder outage. Proposal for patch release v1.3.1:
- dotnet-sdk: reuse HttpClient by default, add auth single-flight
- sample: default paginationConcurrency=4 and SemaphoreSlim usage
- SDK: add jittered exponential backoff on 429s, opt-in client-side token-bucket limiter
- docs: onboarding guide note about reusing client and not creating per-page clients
ci-bot: Created PR #221: "dotnet: pagination window + auth single-flight + jittered retries" in dotnet-sdk repo, CI queued :rocket:
kevin: Let's also add an e2e sim that injects delayed token endpoint and asserts max concurrent auth calls <=2 and no >5 concurrent data requests.
maria: I'll add the test in samples/tests and update the onboarding README with a short checklist.
yoshi: Great. After PR merges, I'll run a 1min load test on staging and monitor request rates.
maria: Thanks team — filing follow-up to check metrics next week and to compare with JS/Python fixes to ensure parity.
